findings.heading: Dashboards with R Markdown
findings.proposition: The Resources section is located at the end of the page.
findings.reader_consequence: The French reader is given a locative claim about where the Resources section sits that the English does not make; harmless if the layout matches, but it is unsourced content added by the translator.

findings.heading: YAML
findings.proposition: The YAML metadata example declares the document title with the key `title:`.
findings.reader_consequence: The French example chunk writes `tite:` instead of `title:`, so a reader who copies the shown metadata block gets a document with no title and no error message pointing at the cause.

findings.heading: YAML
findings.proposition: Inline R code in a YAML value is written with the `r` preceded marker inside BACKTICKS.
findings.reader_consequence: The French text says the `r` goes 'entre guillemets' (within quotes) rather than within backticks, so a reader writes date: "r Sys.Date()" with no backticks and the code is never evaluated; it prints as literal text.

findings.heading: Code chunks
findings.proposition: A code chunk is opened with three backticks followed by CURLY BRACKETS containing a lowercase r.
findings.reader_consequence: The French text says 'parenthèses' (round brackets), so a reader writes ```(r) instead of ```{r}; the chunk is not recognised as R code and never runs.

findings.heading: Narrative text
findings.proposition: Inline R code is inserted into narrative text by surrounding the code with BACKTICKS.
findings.reader_consequence: The French text says to surround the code with 'barres obliques inversées' (backslashes), so a reader writes \r 1+1\ and the inline code is never evaluated.

findings.heading: Narrative text
findings.proposition: The rendered page displays the literal inline-code syntax as an example, escaped so that it is not evaluated.
findings.reader_consequence: The English escapes the example so the reader sees the syntax itself; the French writes it as live inline code, so the rendered page shows the evaluated result instead of the syntax, and the reader never sees the pattern being taught.

findings.heading: Layout
findings.proposition: The YAML parameter `orientation:` takes the literal value `rows` or `columns`.
findings.reader_consequence: The French gives the accepted values as `rangees` or `colonnes`. flexdashboard accepts only the English literals, so a reader who follows this gets a dashboard that ignores the setting or fails to build.

findings.heading: Orientation
findings.proposition: Setting `orientation: columns` in YAML makes second-level headings create columns.
findings.reader_consequence: The French instructs the reader to write `orientation: colonnes` (and gives `orientation: lignes` as the alternative). These are not valid flexdashboard values, so the layout will not change as described. The French code example at line 410 of the same file still uses `orientation: columns`, contradicting its own prose.

findings.heading: Orientation
findings.proposition: Setting `orientation: rows` in YAML makes second-level headings create rows instead of columns.
findings.reader_consequence: The French instructs the reader to write `orientation: lignes`, which flexdashboard does not accept, so the rows layout the paragraph promises is never produced.

findings.heading: Orientation
findings.proposition: The per-page `{data-orientation=}` attribute takes the unquoted value `rows` or `columns`.
findings.reader_consequence: The French tells the reader to specify `lignes` or `colonnes`, so a per-page orientation attribute written from this instruction is invalid. The same French file keeps `rows`/`columns` in the equivalent bullet at line 164, so the reader is given two contradictory value sets.

findings.heading: Tables
findings.proposition: The `options =` argument of `DT::datatable()` is supplied with the R function `list()`.
findings.reader_consequence: The French example chunk writes `options = liste(...)`. `liste` is not an R function, so a reader who copies the block gets 'could not find function "liste"' and no table.

findings.heading: HTML widgets
findings.proposition: The HTML widget package for interactive time series display is named dygraphs.
findings.reader_consequence: The French names it 'digraphs', which is not the package. A reader searching or running install.packages("digraphs") finds nothing.

findings.heading: Settings
findings.proposition: The example YAML header shown for enabling shiny is valid YAML that can be pasted into a flexdashboard script.
findings.reader_consequence: The French example ends the title line with a full stop outside the closing quote (`title: "...".`), which is a YAML parse error. A reader who copies the block cannot render the document and the error points at the header, not at the typo.
